commands.lead: Terminal commands to copy, from Git and npm to Angular, Django and Docker. Each entry briefly says what you need it for.
commands.empty: There are no entries for this topic yet.

what.title: What are commands?
what.text: A command is a line of text you type into the terminal. Instead of clicking through menus, you tell the computer directly what to do: create a folder, install a package, save a state with Git or start a server.

why.title: Why do they matter?
why.text: Many web development tools have no interface to click. You use Git, npm, the Angular CLI, Django and Docker in the terminal. Knowing the most important commands helps you set up projects faster and understand guides and error messages better.

memorize.title: Do you need to know them all by heart?
memorize.text: No. Nobody knows every command by heart, experienced developers look them up too. What matters is that you understand what a command does before you run it. That is why every entry says in one sentence what you need it for.

concepts.lead: The ideas behind the code explained in plain words, each with a short example and what to remember.
concepts.empty: There are no explanations for this topic yet.

what.title: What are basics?
what.text: Basics explain the ideas behind the code: what a loop is, how Flexbox arranges elements, what Docker actually does or why CSS classes are named after BEM. Each explanation is short and comes with an example and what you should remember.

why.title: Why do they matter?
why.text: Anyone can copy code. You can only adapt it, find bugs and explain your decisions once you understand how it works. That is exactly what job interviews ask about.

difference.title: How are they different from terms?
difference.text: Terms give you a short definition to look up. Basics go one step further: they use an example to show how something works and when to use it.

guides.lead: Set up projects cleanly step by step: with the recommended folder structure, an explanation for every step and the code to copy.
guides.roadmapTitle: This is just one step of many
guides.roadmapHint: My project takes you from an empty folder to online, matched to your stack.
guides.empty: There are no guides for this topic yet.

purpose.title: What do the guides help you with?
purpose.text: They help you set up a project cleanly from the start. Not just create and run it, but right away with the folder structure and settings recommended for Angular, Django and the other tools.

structure.title: Why does a good structure matter?
structure.text: A project grows. When folders, files and settings are in the right place from the start, you find your way around faster later, others understand your code, and you do not have to rearrange everything halfway through.

steps.title: How is a guide structured?
steps.text: Each step says what you do and why, and gives you the code to copy. In the end you have a project with a structure you can also explain in a job interview.

debugging.lead: Understand and fix common error messages: what the message means, where it comes from and how to fix it.
debugging.empty: There are no error messages for this topic yet.

message.title: What does an error message tell me?
message.text: Almost always three things: the kind of error, the file and the line. That usually tells you where to look.

start.title: Where do I start?
start.text: With the most important line of the message. Jump to the place it names in your own code and skip lines from packages like node_modules.

stuck.title: What if I get stuck?
stuck.text: Look up the message under your topic in the common errors. If that does not help, narrow the error down with one of the ways under Debugging.

ai.lead: Set up Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity CLI in the terminal and use them in a way that keeps you understanding the code.

what.title: What is AI coding?
what.text: An AI agent works right inside your project. It reads files, suggests changes, runs commands and checks the result. You describe the task, the agent works through it step by step and asks before it does anything important.

why.title: Why is it worth it?
why.text: Agents take routine work off your hands, such as writing tests, narrowing down bugs or restructuring code. That only works well if you know how to describe tasks, which permissions to give the agent and how to check its result.

start.title: Where do I start?
start.text: Pick a tool and set it up. Then create a project file that holds your rules. And never keep code you cannot explain.

notice.title: Coding with AI still means understanding the code.
notice.text: An agent writes fast. Whether the code is right is up to you. Read every change and only keep what you can explain.

faq.lead: Answers to general questions about SnipAtlas: what you'll find here, what you need an account for and how to contact me.

what.question: What is SnipAtlas?
what.answer: A reference for beginners in web development. You'll find commands to copy, basics in plain words, guides for whole projects and help with error messages. The goal: from your first command to a finished project online.

tested.question: Are the commands tested?
tested.answer: Yes. Every command is tried out before it goes on the site. Where the version matters, for example with Angular, it's stated right next to it.

os.question: Why are there commands for Windows and for Linux/Mac?
os.answer: Some commands differ between systems. Choose yours once in the settings, and SnipAtlas shows the matching variant everywhere.

wrong.question: A command is missing or wrong. What can I do?
wrong.answer: Every command, error message and term has a “Report an error” link. It opens the request form with the matching reference. Suggest missing content through the request form.

needed.question: Do I need an account?
needed.answer: The reference and guides are freely accessible. Without an account, guide progress stays in your browser. An account gives you access to My project, favorites, color themes and requests in your profile.

stored.question: What is stored with my account?
stored.answer: Your email address, your password only as a hash, your favorites, your guide progress, your project with progress and notes, your settings and your requests. The details are in the privacy policy.

delete.question: How do I delete my account?
delete.answer: Under Profile, Account. This deletes all data that belongs to your account. You can download your data there first.

project.question: What is "My project"?
project.answer: With an account you can create a personal roadmap. Choose your tools and follow steps with commands, files and the matching folder structure.

free.question: Does SnipAtlas cost anything?
free.answer: No. SnipAtlas is free and without ads. For visitor numbers I use Umami, without cookies and without user profiles.

suggest.question: How do I suggest an entry or an improvement?
suggest.answer: Through the request form. Choose the kind of request and fill in the matching fields. You don't need an account for it.

answer.question: Will I get an answer?
answer.answer: Yes, to the email address you enter in the form. I read every message myself.

privacy.controllerText: The controller for data processing on this website within the meaning of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is:
privacy.hostingText: SnipAtlas runs on a cloud server of Hetzner Online GmbH, Industriestr. 25, 91710 Gunzenhausen, Germany. All data stored by SnipAtlas, for example user accounts and requests, is kept there as well. The server is located in Germany. When you visit SnipAtlas, the server processes technically necessary data such as your IP address in order to deliver the page. The legal basis is Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR. My legitimate interest is providing the website securely and reliably. A data processing agreement pursuant to Art. 28 GDPR is in place with Hetzner.
privacy.logsIntro: On every request, the web server automatically stores the following information transmitted by your browser:

logItems.time: date and time of the request
logItems.status: status code and amount of data transferred

privacy.logsText: I need this data to keep the site running, find errors and fend off attacks. I do not combine it with other data and do not use it for statistics. The log files are deleted automatically after 14 days. The legal basis is Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR.
privacy.resourcesText: The Urbanist and IBM Plex Mono fonts, the icons and the topic logos are stored on my own server and loaded from there. There is no connection to Google Fonts or content delivery networks. The only exception is the visitor statistics with Umami (see the next section).
privacy.analyticsText: SnipAtlas uses the web analytics service Umami Cloud, provided by Umami Software, Inc. (USA). The collected data is stored on servers in the European Union. Umami collects anonymised usage data such as pages visited, time spent on the site, referring website, approximate country of origin, device type, browser and operating system. This helps me understand how SnipAtlas is used and improve it.
privacy.analyticsPrivacy: Umami does not set cookies, does not store any information on your device and does not create cross-device profiles. Your IP address is not stored; it is only used briefly to generate an anonymous, regularly rotating check value. I am not able to identify individual visitors.
privacy.analyticsBasis: The legal basis is Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR; I have a legitimate interest in the anonymised analysis of user behaviour in order to improve SnipAtlas. The data is stored in the EU; however, as the provider is based in the USA, access from the USA cannot be completely ruled out. You can object to the collection by enabling the "Do Not Track" setting in your browser or by using a script blocker.
privacy.cookiesText: SnipAtlas sets no cookies for advertising, analytics or tracking. When you sign in, SnipAtlas stores a cookie with a sign-in token in your browser. It keeps you signed in so you do not have to sign in again on every visit. The cookie is deleted when you sign out, at the latest after 14 days. Without signing in, SnipAtlas sets no cookies.
privacy.cookiesBasis: This cookie is strictly necessary for signing in (§ 25 (2) no. 2 TDDDG), so no consent is required. The legal basis for processing is Art. 6 (1) (b) GDPR.
privacy.storageIntro: So that SnipAtlas remembers your settings, the site stores the following in your browser's local storage:
privacy.storageText: This information stays on your device and is not sent to me. You can delete it at any time in your browser settings. If you are signed in, your settings are also stored in your account (see user account). Storing it in the browser is strictly necessary for the function you requested (§ 25 (2) no. 2 TDDDG), so no consent is required. The legal basis for processing is Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR.
privacy.accountText: You need an account for My project and other personal features. To register, you enter your email address and a password. The password is only stored as a hash, I cannot read it.
privacy.accountIntro: For your account, I store the following on the server:

accountItems.login: email address, password hash, whether the address is confirmed, a new address that is not confirmed yet, date of registration and of your last sign-in
accountItems.settings: your settings (commands for Windows or Linux/Mac, email when a request is answered)
accountItems.requests: your requests with their status and my reply
accountItems.project: your project in "My project": the chosen building blocks, the completed steps and your notes on the steps

privacy.accountBasis: The legal basis is Art. 6 (1) (b) GDPR, because I cannot provide the features of your account without this data. Only you can see and change your data. In your account you can change your email address and password and download all your data.
privacy.accountDeletion: You can delete your account yourself at any time. All data belonging to your account is then deleted. If you do not confirm your email address within 7 days of registering, the account is deleted automatically.
privacy.requestBefore: When you write to me using the
privacy.requestAfter: , I process the information you enter there: the type of request, your input in the fields (for example topic, description, example or source, and for bug reports optionally your browser and device) and your email address. The data is transmitted to my server in encrypted form and stored there as a request that only I can work on. I only use it to handle your request and reply to you, and I do not pass it on.
privacy.requestAccount: If you are signed in, I also store the request in your account. Under “My requests” you can then see its status and my reply.
privacy.requestBasis: The legal basis is your consent pursuant to Art. 6 (1) (a) GDPR, which you give by ticking the checkbox in the form. You can withdraw it at any time with effect for the future. A short email is enough.
privacy.requestDeletion: I automatically delete requests sent without an account 6 months after they have been dealt with, or earlier if you ask for it to be deleted or withdraw your consent. Requests in your account remain visible there until you delete your account. Statutory retention obligations remain unaffected.
privacy.mailsText: SnipAtlas only sends you emails that you trigger yourself: a link to confirm your account when you register, and a notice if there already is an account for your address. Also a link to confirm a new email address when you change it, a link to reset your password when you request one, and a notification when I reply to your request and you have switched this on. I do not send newsletters or advertising. The legal basis for the emails about your account is Art. 6 (1) (b) GDPR, for the notification your consent pursuant to Art. 6 (1) (a) GDPR. You can switch it off in your settings at any time.
privacy.mailsProvider: To send all emails from SnipAtlas, I use the Resend service of Plus Five Five, Inc., USA. Resend processes your email address and the content of the email for this purpose. The data may be transferred to the USA. Plus Five Five, Inc. is certified under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, so the transfer is covered by the European Commission's adequacy decision (Art. 45 GDPR). Standard contractual clauses are also in place (Art. 46 (2) (c) GDPR). A data processing agreement pursuant to Art. 28 GDPR is in place with Resend.
privacy.emailText: When you email me directly, I process your email address and the content of your message in order to reply. The legal basis is Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR. My legitimate interest is answering your message. I delete it once your matter has been dealt with.
privacy.tlsText: SnipAtlas is only delivered over an encrypted connection (HTTPS with TLS). You can recognise it by “https://” in your browser's address bar. This prevents third parties from reading the data you transmit.
privacy.rightsIntro: You have the right at any time to:

rightItems.access: access the data stored about you (Art. 15 GDPR)
rightItems.complaint: lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority (Art. 77 GDPR), for example the supervisory authority of Lower Saxony

privacy.rightsText: To do so, simply email me at the address above.
privacy.changesText: I will update this policy whenever something changes on SnipAtlas that affects your data. The version on this page always applies.

home.title: From an empty folder to online
home.text: Choose frontend, backend or both. You get your roadmap step by step, matched to your stack.

intro.lead: You have an idea for a web app. Which folders do you need first, and when does the database come in? Your roadmap follows the choices you make for your project.
intro.title: A task board with Angular and Django
intro.example: On your board, tasks move from “Open” to “Done”. You choose Angular for the interface and Django for the API. Choose PostgreSQL to store the tasks and your roadmap adds the database setup steps.
intro.sample: Inside a step: Create the Django project
intro.command: Django is installed and your terminal is in backend/. The dot at the end of the command creates the project in that folder. Look for manage.py to check that you ran it in the right place.

items.backend: Set up the backend with Django
items.frontend: Set up the frontend with Angular

intro.progress: You set up Django and started your server on port 8000. Check off the step and leave yourself a note with the port number. When you return, your overview shows the next unfinished step and you can revisit your note.

myProject.missing: This step is not part of your roadmap. Set up your project or go back to the overview.
